title: The Tale of Attaf

full_text:
In Damascus lived Attaf, a wealthy nobleman celebrated for his peerless hospitality and magnanimity.
One winter, Vizier Ja'afar the Barmecide, having incurred the temporary displeasure of Caliph Harun al-Rashid, traveled disguised to Damascus to seek refuge.
Without knowing his guest's royal identity, Attaf welcomed the stranger into his palace, treated him like an emperor for four months, and provided him with every comfort.

While walking in Damascus, Ja'afar caught sight of an exquisite lady in a garden pavilion and fell deeply into melancholy longing.
When Attaf noticed his guest's wasting sorrow, he inquired about the cause. When Ja'afar described the house and the maiden, Attaf realized with a shock that the maiden was his own betrothed, whom he loved dearly!

Yet such was Attaf's sublime commitment to sacred friendship and hospitality that he concealed his own heartbreak. He quietly broke his betrothal, endowed the maiden with a lavish dowry, and arranged her honorable marriage to his guest, sending them safely back to Baghdad!

Years later, Attaf's fortunes turned through commercial betrayals and false lawsuits. Stripped of his wealth, Attaf wandered to Baghdad as a destitute beggar, wearing a ragged cloak.
Caught in a city sweep after a midnight robbery, Attaf was falsely accused and brought before the Grand Vizier for sentencing.

Seated upon the tribunal was Ja'afar!
Ja'afar looked at the ragged prisoner, recognized the noble features of his Damascene benefactor, and leaped down from the judge's bench with tears streaming from his eyes!
He embraced Attaf before the entire court, shouting:
'This is Attaf! The man who sacrificed his own happiness to preserve mine!'

Ja'afar brought Attaf before Caliph Harun al-Rashid, recounting the entire history of Attaf's peerless generosity.
The Caliph was moved to tears by such rare nobility of spirit.
He decreed that Attaf be appointed Governor of Damascus, restored all his ancestral estates with tenfold interest, and presented him with royal honors.
Attaf returned to Syria in glory, remembered throughout the centuries as the supreme exemplar of magnanimous friendship.
moral: True friendship is founded on supreme selflessness; generosity rendered in secret returns as salvation in the hour of need.
